summary: Regex detectors found seven structural properties that split sample labels perfectly in every probe; the corpus showed them independent. Per-probe latent contributions were gradient times class-mean activation shift. Heuristic labelling of candidates from corpus examples was dropped. For each probe, true logits on two synthetic notes (each topic written in the other class's style) gave the topic effect T and the total style effect S. Latents were labelled by the sign pattern of their class shift across the four probes. Each property's share was summed contribution, rescaled by 10/net, divided by T. The cue was the largest helpful share. Ablation sets were pattern-filtered latents, token-checked and checked with probe_scores ablation.

phases.purpose: Read the sample notes and compare label balance and the class-0 and class-1 note formats for each probe.
Regex detectors for 7 structural and 4 free properties; per-class rates; flag properties with near-perfect splits.
Corpus marginals and pairwise correlation of the detectors, to confirm the properties are independent.

Gradient x class-mean shift decomposition per probe; compare F@g with the scored logits; regress the residual on the reconstruction and check free properties against it; take the union of the top 25 |contrib| latents per probe.
Corpus examples (n=4, then n=10) for the 72 candidates; property fractions and token-vote labelling; a fixed-group property/topic ratio (later dropped).
Per-token view of the top ambiguous latents on one note per class (gave no clear separation).
Class-mean anchors from sample notes; template generator; true logits on 2 conflict notes per probe; estimate T, S and S/T.
Label latents by cosine of their 4-probe class-shift vector to each property's class-sign pattern; compute per-property share contrib*scale/T; sweep the cos thresholds.
Token check of greeting/exclaim/gender/case/bullet/hashtag latents; final share table over helpful (positive) contributions; assign a cue per probe.
Exclaim-axis and gender-axis candidate lists ranked by |contrib|; token-level check on one note of each class; widened search.
Ablation separation checks for the gender and exclaim sets, greeting vs case group ablations on probe 0, cos-band contribution sums, a 16-latent exclaim set with token check, wider gender search.
Build the answer, test the regexes on toy strings, submit.

probe_query_use.purpose: estimate topic effect T and total style effect S = 10 - T from class-mean anchors

template notes: photography in astronomy-class style; astronomy in photography-class style

per_probe.procedure: The conflict-note logits gave a moderate total style/topic ratio. Latents were labelled by the cosine of their cross-probe class-shift pattern. Among high-cos latents, exclaim had the largest helpful share. Case latents pushed against the label, and both their share and their ablation (which raised separation) ruled case out. Greeting was a close second in share and in ablation drop. Cos-band sums favoured exclaim at high cos, and greeting's mid-cos mass was put down to astronomy-topic latents. Latents came from exclaim-axis candidates ranked by |contrib0| and token-checked on one note of each class, keeping punctuation-firing ones. Regex: a literal '!'.
per_probe.quote: **probe0 = exclaim** (largest helpful signal ~0.26→≥0.3; greeting only 0.11 clean; upper is counterproductive=not a cue)

per_probe.procedure: The conflict-note true logits gave a small total style/topic ratio. Pattern-labelled latent shares were all small, the largest being greeting at about 0.11-0.19, which the session judged unreliable because it exceeded the measured total. With both the measured ratio and every property share low, the answer was none.

The conflict-note logits gave the largest style/topic ratio. The pattern-labelled share was dominated by the gender pattern, carried mostly by a few pronoun latents. Candidates were sign-consistent across all four probes and ranked by |contrib2|. They were token-checked on one fishing note and one gardening note, keeping latents that fire on pronouns with no topic words. Wider searches found no more pronoun latents, so the set stayed at 4. An ablation separation check on the sample notes was run before submitting. Regex: word-bounded he|his|him, case-insensitive.

Both conflict-note true logits matched the class anchors, so S was near zero and S/T was slightly negative. This settled it as none before any latent localization. Later share tables showed small gender and case shares, and these were not acted on.

decision_points.choice: Hand-written regex detectors from reading notes; kept the properties whose class rates split near-perfectly in the samples (7 structural); free properties used only as controls.
decision_points.quote: Set **S = {gender, case, bullet, greeting, signature, hashtag, exclaim}** — 7 structural properties perfectly correlated with label in every sample.

decision_points.choice: A programmatic template generator holding free properties fixed. Per probe, one note of each topic was written in the opposite class's full style bundle (all structural properties swapped together, none alone).
decision_points.quote: Now let me build a generator mimicking the note style and create conflict notes (Qb=topic1+style0, Qref2=topic0+style1) per probe to measure topic coefficient T directly.

decision_points.choice: Total style effect came from true logits against class-mean anchors. The per-property split used gradient x class-shift contributions of pattern-labelled latents, rescaled by 10/net and divided by T. probe_scores ablation was a secondary check.
2 conflict notes per probe for all 4 probes, all spent in one round before any localization.
None when the measured S/T is near zero (probe 3), or when it is small and every pattern-labelled property share is at or below ~0.15 (probe 1).
decision_points.quote: **probe1 = none**: S/T=0.15, all properties ≤0.15 (clean greeting only 0.11).

decision_points.choice: Each latent was matched to a property by the cosine between its class-shift vector across the 4 probes and that property's class-sign pattern, which differs between probes. Only properties with a helpful (positive) contribution were counted, and anti-collinear patterns were told apart by tokens.
decision_points.quote: a latent detecting property X has a class-difference (dF) whose **sign pattern across the 4 probes matches X's known property→class mapping**

decision_points.choice: A competing property was rejected when ablating its latent group increased separation.
decision_points.quote: Case is counterproductive (ablating it *increases* separation) — so not a cue.

decision_points.choice: Written by hand from the detector definitions: a literal '!' and a case-insensitive word-bounded he|his|him. Each was checked on a few toy strings, one positive and one or two negatives.
decision_points.quote: print('  tricky(the/this/shed):', bool(re.search(g,'the garden is this shed')))

decision_points.choice: Filter on property-pattern cosine and shift norm, rank by |contrib| for the target probe, then keep the latents whose top activating tokens on one note of each class are the cue tokens. The final exclaim set was a hand-picked 6. The gender set was the 3 pronoun latents plus 8679.
decision_points.quote: L9330, L6871 (pure "!"), L12020 (pure "."), L12924 (punctuation) are clean. Others carry hashtag/bullet/topic — exclude.

decision_points.choice: probe_scores mean-ablation on the sample notes, comparing class separation before and after. The regexes were tested on toy strings. No true-logit check was run after ablation.
decision_points.quote: confirm ablating my gender/exclaim latents removes the cue's share of separation while preserving topic separation.

decision_points.choice: Two probes with one cue each (6 latents and 4 latents); two probes answered none.
The scored logits were checked against the latent reconstruction F@g. The residual (the SAE error term) tracked the reconstruction, so contribution ratios were taken as valid.
decision_points.quote: the error term is ~proportional to the latent reconstruction (err ≈ 1.09·est, per-note corr 0.92)

decision_points.choice: The heuristic token-vote and property-fraction classifiers were dropped in favour of cross-probe pattern matching.

caveats: Most bash/tool outputs are truncated in the log, so exact candidate lists, some shares and the n=10 classification table are only partly visible. The final exclaim list keeps 7503 and 10390 even though a NOTE called non-pure latents excluded; it is encoded as a constant. 8679 in the gender set was never shown as a pattern-matched candidate. The decision rule for picking the cue (largest helpful share, cross-checked by ablation drop and cos bands) is applied by judgment, not as a coded threshold. The reconstruction check was done for probe 0 only. Synthetic texts swap all style properties together, so true-logit measurement gives only total style per probe.
